query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying HfNbTaTiZr with 0.5 at.% Si will improve its high-temperature oxidation resistance without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective silica scale
generation.mechanism: Improved oxidation resistance due to the formation of a protective silica scale
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxidation resistance without sacrificing mechanical performance
generation.boundary: 1000 °C, air, 100 hours, mechanical loading at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the silica scale in improving oxidation resistance and the potential impact on mechanical properties
generation.falsification_experiment: Exposure of alloyed and unalloyed HfNbTaTiZr to 1000 °C in air for 100 hours, followed by tensile testing at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
